newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: PRESS DIGEST - CENTRAL/EAST EUROPE - JAN 9.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - CENTRAL/EAST EUROPE - JAN 9.

text.p: HOSPODARSKE NOVINY - In a meeting in April, the cabinet will decide about strategic investors for Aero Vodochody a.s.. The tender will be open to domestic and foreign candidates and will be advertised.

- The proposal from the Industry and Trade Ministry about government policy on exports was approved yesterday in a cabinet meeting. It contains no changes on exchange rate policy, increases on export tariffs nor any kind of restrictive measures for imports, but suggests improvements for corporate financial situations.
- Pharmeceutical companies have recently decreased their prices. Some insurance companies have reacted by reducing their reimbursments for certain medicines.
MLADA FRONTA DNES - Inflation in 1996 was much calmer than expected. According to still unofficial information, the medium year inflation rate reached 8.6 percent.
- Political parties had profits last year of at least 60 million crowns, double the previous year.
- The cabinet, for the second time, did not approve the proposal from the Regional Development Ministry on housing politics.

PRAVO - According to a new law approved Wednesday by the cabinet concerning inheritance and donation taxes from realty transfers, close relatives do not have inheritance or donation taxes on realty up to one million crowns.

- Although in November the Czech Statistics Office predicted an increase of nearly seven percent for the whole of 1996, the increase will probably be closer to the lower estimate from July of a maximum of 5.6 percent.
-- Prague Newsroom, 42-2-2423-0003 NARODNA OBRODA - The three Slovaks kidnapped last October in Ingushenia, near Chechnya, are expected to be released soon.
- Czech car maker Skoda ranked first in sales in Slovakia last year, selling 23,035 cars. Skoda said it planned to increase its Slovak exports to 25,000 units in 1997.

- Skoda imported components, mainly steel sheets from VSZ and tyres from Matador Puchov, worth about three billion crowns in Slovakia last year, and said it planned to increase deliveries to 3.8 billion crowns in 1997.

- Czech parliamentary chairman Milos Zeman will pay a two day visit to Slovakia, starting on January 15. Zeman is scheduled to meet his Slovak counterpart Ivan Gasparovic, President Michal Kovac and Prime Minister Vladimir Meciar.

HOSPODARSKE NOVINY - Faster growth of the foreign trade deficit in November and the expected surge in imports at the end of the year rae expected to push the Slovak foreign trade shortfall beyond the forecasted 52 billion crowns in 1996.
- Overall investment to hydro projetcs, including planned river dams, are expected to total 3.7 billion crowns this year.
- Slovakia and Ukraine have so far created 200 joint- venture companies.
- Heavy engineering company Povazske Strojarne said it planned to widen its sales network abroad, mainly towards western Europe, from its current sales offices in Russia, Romania and Bulgaria
SME - Transport Minister Alexander Rezes said he was considering to resign in the near future.

- The opposition Party of Democratic Left (SDL) opposed attempts of other opposition parties to initiate a refendem to change the presidential electoral system to a direct citizen vote. The SDL said that such a change would be unconstitutional and that it might bring the case to the constitutional court. -- Bratislava Newsroom, 42-7-563-3687
The following are the main stories from Thursday morning's Austrian newspapers:
DER STANDARD

- EA-Generali led consortium improves its offer for Creditanstalt. A decision on the sale of the government's 70 percent voting stake is expected by Friday, and top leaders of the coalition government are planning a special emergency meeting on the sale next Monday. Chancellor Franz Vranitzky says the coalition will not collapse.
- Opposition parties are against suggestions by the conservative People's Party to privatise Creditanstalt by selling the bank's shares on the stock exchange.
- People's Party chief whip Andreas Khol says his party will not leave the coalition with the dominant Social Democrats, says new elections are out of the question.
- VA Krems, a unit of steelmaker VA Stahl, will invest 100 million schillings in a production plant in the Czech Republic.
- Austrian regions oppose Economy Minister Hannes Farnleitner's plans to reorganise Austria's electricity market.
- Flag-carrier Austrian Airlines to start closer cooperation on transatlantic routes with Swissair, Belgium's Sabena and U.S. carrier Delta on February 1.
- Some 100 billion schillings were invested in Austrian investment funds last year, raising the total volume invested to 440 billion schillings.
- Average 1996 unemployment total has risen to 231,000 from 216,000 in the year before.
DIE PRESSE
- Dominant Social Democrats and conservative junior coalition partner People's Party, holding seperate annual congresses, dig in heels over the sale of Creditanstalt.
- People's Party wants to spend an extra 12 billion schillings on family support payments in 1999, financed through a tax reform.
- Social Democrats say they won't be bullied into a decision on the sale of Creditanstalt by the conservatives.
- A decision for Bank Austria in the race for Creditanstalt coudl be expected by Friday, sources close to the talks say.
- Austrian beer sales expected to remain flat this year due to bad weather, slow tourism season and rising illegal imports of beer, Association of Austrian Brewers said.
- About 44 percent of Austrians believe the country's economic situation will continue to deteriorate, new study shows. Only one third of Austrians believe the situation will remain unchanged.
KURIER
- Longer shop opening hours introduced at the start of the year have helped to create a rising number of jobs, most of them part-time, in Austria's retail industry.
- Post & Telekom Austria, the state-owned telecoms monopoly, says it plans to lower telephone charges by 1998.
- Economic research institute Wifo expects Austrian tourism income to fall by one percent in 1997, sees "stagnation on a high level".
